page.title: Privacy
page.intro: Your Health Information. Your Control. Explore consent concepts below, then use the session demo if you are testing the mock API.
page.demo: This session is a demonstration. The switches below send consent changes to the mock API used in this build. They do not provide production backend security and are not legally effective consent.
page.controlsLead: Each switch records a consent change in this session. Turn a share off to revoke it. Your own result stays on.
page.revokeLead: Revoke uses the existing confirm dialog. The previous choice is restored if the request fails.

empty: No sharing details are available for this session.
error: Privacy details could not be loaded.

explain.heading: What this page covers
explain.lead: Sharing is limited to the scopes this product already implements. Research aggregate is listed because the mock matrix includes it, not because a research pipeline is live.

own.title: Your own result
own.body: You can always see your own result in this session. That switch stays on and cannot be turned off here.

overlap.title: Overlap with your partner
overlap.body: When this is on, the overlap note can appear on Results. When it is off, that note is withheld in this session.

clinic.title: Clinic share
clinic.body: When this is on, the Care page can send a referral through the existing pathway API. When it is off, that send stays blocked.

research.title: Research aggregate
research.body: The matrix shows this row as a placeholder. This build does not implement a research share or a research audience.

matrix.caption: Who can see this
matrix.partnerSwitch: Share the overlap with your partner

revoke.title: Revoke this share?
revoke.failed: The share could not be changed. The previous choice is restored.

receipt.heading: Receipts
receipt.lead: Each consent change in this session can be downloaded as JSON. The files are the existing receipt records.

audit.heading: Who accessed my data
audit.lead: This list is the access log already recorded for the session. It is not a live security monitor.
audit.empty: No access is recorded for this session.

education.heading: Your Health Information. Your Control.
education.intro: Genetic and family health information can be deeply personal. Rafeeq is designed around individual choice, clear consent and careful information sharing.
education.prototypeNotice: Prototype interaction – changes are not saved and no information is shared.
education.notProductionSecurity: These principles describe product intent. They are not a claim that production-grade security is active in this demo build.

principles.title: Individual control
principles.body: Each person should be able to make their own decisions about sharing personal health information.

principles.title: Explicit consent
principles.body: Information should only be shared when the relevant individual has clearly authorized the intended sharing.

principles.title: Limited access
principles.body: Sharing should be limited to the information and purpose the individual has selected.

principles.title: Transparency
principles.body: Individuals should be able to understand what information is intended to be shared and with whom.

matrix.heading: Consent matrix (visual prototype)
matrix.lead: Sample categories show how granular consent might look. Toggles affect only this page in memory.
matrix.caption: Prototype consent matrix
matrix.memoryOnly: States exist only in memory until you leave this page.

rows.purpose: Track which Learn topics you opened in the app demo
rows.explanation: Does not share genetic results; not stored on a server in this prototype.
Would share only summary fields you select—not full raw data—in a future integration.
Each partner chooses independently; invitation alone does not grant access.
Questions you draft in Care preview are not submitted in this build.

minimization.heading: Share Only What Is Needed
minimization.body: Information sharing should be limited to what is relevant for the specific purpose. An individual should not need to share their entire personal or family health history simply to access educational support.
